clue.text: Join together in company with drinks before church

indicators.note: before places the earlier words ahead of the final one in the written order

blocks.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company
ales are beers, drinks served in a pub
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A group of friends gathers for a few drinks before heading off to a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To coalesce is to merge or unite into one mass, so it is a direct synonym of combining into a whole.

clue.text: Element about work upset agent

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
OP is short for opus, a musical work
a rep is a sales representative or agent

explanation.surface: A chemical element seems to be about a job that has unsettled an undercover agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is a metallic chemical element, atomic number 29, so the answer is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Devices for slowing down broadcast? Pauses in speech

indicators.note: in speech means we take the word as it is spoken, not as it is written

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
breaks are pauses, and the word is said the same as another spelling

explanation.surface: A question about slowing a broadcast down, answered by the pauses a presenter makes while talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Air brakes are braking systems worked by compressed air, used on lorries and trains to bring them to a stop.

clue.text: Always handy, went on working periodically

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are set in motion and put into a new arrangement

blocks.note: ever means always, as in ever-ready
the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dependable helper who kept going on with the job, if only from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Every now and then is an idiom for occasionally, at intervals, which is what periodically describes.

clue.text: Outstanding lesson

blocks.note: first meaning: excellent
second meaning: a period of teaching at school

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like praise for a lesson, but the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word is an adjective for first-rate quality, and as a noun it names a school teaching session.

clue.text: Device for calculating area covered initially in a vehicle

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of the preceding word
in places the earlier pieces inside the following words

blocks.note: taken as written
a bus is a road vehicle
A is the abbreviation for area
the opening letter of covered

explanation.surface: A calculator that works out an area, as if measured by a passenger riding in a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The insert is two letters taken together, the area abbreviation plus the opening letter of 'covered'; the leading 'a' stays outside the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads on rods used for doing arithmetic by hand, an early counting instrument.

clue.text: Cut rebuke of that complicated film about time travel

indicators.note: complicated means tangled up, so the letters are mixed into another order

blocks.note: all fifteen letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film editor trims a scolding speech from a convoluted time-travel movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Back to the Future is the 1985 Robert Zemeckis movie in which Marty McFly journeys to 1955 in a DeLorean.

clue.text: Tea? New range

blocks.note: chai is a spiced tea, and a word for tea generally
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone asks for tea, and is shown a new line of products.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of mountains is a range, a connected series of peaks running in a line.

clue.text: Freeze sauce to retain top condition

indicators.note: to retain is to hold onto, so the first word keeps the others inside it

blocks.note: soy is the salty sauce made from fermented beans
a lid is the top of a jar or pot
if introduces a condition, as in 'ifs and buts'

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice: freeze the sauce so it keeps in peak condition.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeze a liquid is to make it set hard, turning it from liquid to solid form.

clue.text: Separate northern takeover, in principle, not right

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the following letter from the word before
in puts the earlier words inside the shortened word that follows

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
a coup is a sudden seizure of power
a principle is a rule
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Splitting up a hostile northern takeover, at least in theory, would not be the right thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In principle' looks like a phrase meaning theoretically, but 'principle' is a synonym to shorten, and 'in' tells where the takeover goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncouple is to disconnect two linked things, such as railway carriages, so to part them.

clue.text: China, clear about power, ignoring France

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word wraps the second
ignoring means leaving out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: plain means clear, obvious
force is power or strength
F is the international code for France

explanation.surface: A plain statement about political power in which France is left out.
explanation.walkthrough: China with a capital looks like the country; here it is crockery, so the capital is just the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine ceramic tableware is called china, after the country where it was first made, a synonym for this ware.

clue.text: Car may well, at regular intervals, move slowly

indicators.note: regular intervals means every other letter is picked out, skipping the rest

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A car may well inch along in traffic every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: To crawl is to proceed at a snail's pace, as traffic does in a jam.

clue.text: Nobleman unknown in advance

blocks.note: an earl is a British peer
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: An aristocrat whose identity is not known beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something early means doing it ahead of time, before it is due, so the phrase fits adverbially.

clue.text: Reduced number in coastal region by day

indicators.note: in puts the number inside the region that follows
by means next to, so the last piece is set alongside

blocks.note: the shore is the land along the sea
ten is a number
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Fewer people were on the coast by day, the numbers cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shortened has been made briefer or cut down, matching reduced as a past participle.

clue.text: Easily outdo spies, sour after setback

indicators.note: after places the earlier words behind the last one in the written order

blocks.note: a knock is a blow or setback
to spy something is to spot it
milk that has turned sour has gone off

explanation.surface: Spies turn bitter after their mission suffers a reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Setback is not a reversal signal here; it is just a blow. Read 'spies' as a verb and 'sour' as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock spots off someone is a British idiom for beating them comprehensively, being far superior.

clue.text: Spring up, diving into gift bag

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from the bottom to the top
diving into means plunging inside, so one word goes into the other

blocks.note: a knack is a natural gift or talent
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Jumping up, someone plunges into a present to find a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A knapsack is a backpack, a cloth or leather pouch carried on the shoulders.

clue.text: Nothing pleasant about silly hint in a risky situation

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the pleasant word wraps the rearranged one
silly suggests letters behaving foolishly, jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
nice means pleasant
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nothing nice to say about a foolish hint, which leaves you exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on thin ice is an idiom for being in a precarious position, where one wrong step causes trouble.

clue.text: Hand in a legal document, not English? It's accepted

indicators.note: not means leaving out the following letter from the document word
in means the hand goes inside the remaining letters

blocks.note: taken as written
a deed is a signed legal document
E is the abbreviation for English
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Submit a legal paper that isn't in English and it is still received.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the document's two Es is dropped; 'hand' reads as a verb meaning submit but is the noun, slang for a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: If something is admitted it has been allowed in or acknowledged as true, matching accepted as a past participle.

clue.text: Ridicule inspector and anger people in quarrel

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the last one

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
a spat is a petty quarrel
rage is fierce anger
men are people

explanation.surface: A police inspector stirs up fury between people locked in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparagement is belittling criticism, the act of mocking or speaking scornfully of someone.

clue.text: Off course since daylight's last gleam

indicators.note: last tells us to take only the closing letter of the word

blocks.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it was late'
the final letter of daylight
a ray is a gleam or beam of light

explanation.surface: Lost at sea since the final glimmer of daylight faded.
explanation.definitionFit: To go astray is to wander from the proper path or route, to be lost.

clue.text: Arrogance in memo I'd amended with pen

indicators.note: amended means altered, so the letters are changed into a new order

blocks.note: these letters are rearranged
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A haughty tone crept into the memo I had edited with my pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Immodesty is boastfulness or a lack of humility, close in sense to conceit.

clue.text: Neighbourhood style, according to report

indicators.note: according to report means as heard, going by what is said out loud

blocks.note: manner means style, and is said much the same as another word

explanation.surface: A district's character, as others describe it.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a manor is someone's home patch or local area, especially a police officer's or criminal's.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang usage makes manor one's district or territory, the local area someone knows and controls.

clue.text: Adolescent diary finally published? Hard to support that

indicators.note: finally tells us to take only the closing letter of the word
in a down clue, a piece that supports goes underneath the rest

blocks.note: the final letter of diary
a book that is out has been published
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A teenager's diary at last in print? That would be hard to back.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young person, a teenager, so the noun matches adolescent used as a noun.

clue.text: Modules among best in use, on reflection

indicators.note: among says the letters sit within the following words
a reflection shows things mirror-wise, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: letters running across the word break

explanation.surface: Choosing the best components in service after some thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Units and modules are both self-contained parts of a larger system or course, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Unpleasant smell, not first to indicate fish

indicators.note: not first says the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: a stench is a foul smell

explanation.surface: A nasty odour, rather than anything else, is the sign of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family found in European lakes and ponds.

clue.text: One delivering messages around Utah for designer

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the first word wraps the state

blocks.note: a courier delivers messages and parcels
UT is the postal abbreviation for Utah

explanation.surface: A messenger travelling around Utah on behalf of a fashion house.
explanation.walkthrough: The state abbreviation sits after the messenger's first two letters, not in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A couturier is a fashion designer who makes high-quality custom clothing, a French term.

clue.text: Bold call led by lawyer

indicators.note: led by means the following piece goes in front

blocks.note: a DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: A brave phone call made at the urging of an attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring describes someone adventurous and fearless, willing to take risks, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Stealing hearts during match, especially

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the suit goes inside

blocks.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games
very means especially, extremely

explanation.surface: Romance blossoms during a game, notably by hearts being stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Thievery is the act of theft, taking what belongs to others, so it is a noun synonym.
